summary: Phase 12 complete. THE FIRST OF THE TWO GENUINELY HARD SITES HELD. negFixOneFaithful_cover's Case1/Case2/Case3a/b/c split survived the re-base onto HasFaithfulDedekindINF with no case introduced, merged or removed and with its branch structure textually unchanged: a carrier-free by_cases on occurrence wrapping a TWO-ARM rcases on the carrier, Case 3's three arms untouched. The chartered R11 fallback is NOT triggered. Zero failed proof attempts; scoped build green on the FIRST attempt; no proof-search tool invoked at any point. The plan's mandated first task -- transcribing Rabinovich's Lemma 5.1 case enumeration (PDF p.9) and the eq (5.3) use-site guard printed twice (PDF p.10) into the module docstring, stating which K+ makes the split exhaustive -- was landed as the dispatch's FIRST edit, before any tactic was touched, with both p.10 printings re-confirmed verbatim against the corpus. HasFaithfulDedekindINF.first_occ_tp added ADDITIVELY beside a retained, unweakened HasDedekindINF.first_occ_tp (the two are incomparable). negFixOneCase1 -> kplusOpenLeftBlock and infPinPoint -> kplusOpenPred. D3's coercion at :253 removed as chartered. Full lake build green (1919 jobs, 0 errors), sorry-free, axiom-clean, all three canaries unchanged, all frozen assets byte-identical.

hard_site_verdict.detail: Under HasFaithfulDedekindINF the cover's structure is UNCHANGED: `by_cases h_occ` (carrier-free, the paper's Case 2 against the rest) wrapping `rcases h_INF.first_occ_tp s0.neg ... with hk | <r0, ...>` -- exactly TWO arms, no third disjunct, no endpoint by_cases, no added hypothesis -- with Case 3's `by_cases hQ` / `by_cases hs1r` sub-split (arms 3a/3b/3c) textually untouched. The entire code-bearing delta inside the cover is four tokens: the binder type; `kplusLeftBlock_holds` -> `kplusOpenLeftBlock_holds` in the Case 1 arm; and `Or.inr h` -> `Or.inr (kplusOpen_of_kplus h)` in the pin construction, where the carrier's right disjunct still prints the tree's `kplus` (it is literally HasDedekindINF's) while eq (5.3)'s pin type now reads the source's K+. That last insertion is a WEAKENING, so nothing is assumed there that the carrier did not already supply. negFixOneFaithful_sound took the mirror-image change in its Case 1 arm: `obtain <-, hdense> := h1` collapses to applying h1 directly, kplusOpen having no first conjunct to discard -- the same class-b pattern Phase 11 measured at orderedPointsExist_combine_kplusOpen.
hard_site_verdict.why_it_held_not_luck: Rabinovich's enumeration is exhaustive BECAUSE his K+ is conjunct-free. He prints the governing implication twice on PDF p.10 -- as the guard on r0's existence and as Case 3's closed form -- and both say `not-K+(not-b1)(z0)` plus an occurrence yields the pin; contrapositively, an occurrence yields `K+(not-b1)(z0)` OR the pin, a DICHOTOMY. Under the tree's kplus the split is NOT exhaustive: where not-b1 holds at z0 and recurs arbitrarily soon, the source's K+ fires Case 1 while kplus fails at its first conjunct and the infimum is not strictly inside, forcing a third endpoint disjunct `not-b1(z0)` -- literally HasDenseDedekindINF's shape (DedekindINFDense.lean:222) -- for which the paper has no case. This is now transcribed in the module docstring and grounded on three landed declarations (kplusOpen_not_implied_by_truth_at, HasDenseDedekindINF's shape, hasFaithfulDedekindINF_survives_interval_witness), not asserted.
hard_site_verdict.scope_limit: This settles the ONE-WITNESS hard site. It does NOT settle negFixListFaithful_iff (NegFixListFaithful.lean:333/:446 region), whose list-form induction is Phase 12.1's territory. Evidence transfers as STRONG ENCOURAGEMENT -- the same carrier, the same case names, and now a same-shaped site already landed -- but still NOT PROOF; 12.1 must transcribe rather than assume.

transitive_cascade.how_handled: Deviation D4: `Or.inr hkr` -> `Or.inr (kplusOpen_of_kplus hkr)` at the argument position only, plus a five-line SCHEDULED FOR REMOVAL comment. Nothing else in that module changed -- not one binder, statement, docstring or other proof step; its declaration inventory is byte-identical. Its h_INF binder remains HasDedekindINF, so Phase 12.1 re-bases it exactly as planned.
transitive_cascade.warning_performance: 11.1's standing warning was CORRECT that the cascade recurs, and its prescribed check found the site. But the SHAPE it predicted (an argument-position .toHasFaithfulDedekindINF, as in D3) was not the shape that fired. What fired came from the DEFINITION move (infPinPoint -> kplusOpenPred), not the binder move; D3's four existing coercions at :368, :421, :437, :500 stayed green and untouched, because this phase did not re-base negBoundedLeftFixAnchoredFaithful_iff.
transitive_cascade.generalized_warning_for_12_1_and_13: A re-base cascades along TWO INDEPENDENT EDGES -- moved binders and moved definitions -- and a probe or grep aimed at one will not reveal the other. Here the binder edge cost nothing downstream and the definition edge cost one site. Additionally: unlike D3's coercions, D4's will NOT be enforced away by the build, since the weakening stays type-correct under either carrier. It is marked in-file with SCHEDULED FOR REMOVAL and a checklist item was added to Phase 12.1.

declaration_preservation.conclusions_honest_statement: Two DEFINITIONS moved to the source's operator as this phase's charter directs -- negFixOneCase1 (kplusLeftBlock -> kplusOpenLeftBlock) and infPinPoint (kplusPred -> kplusOpenPred) -- which makes negFixOneFaithful a formally weaker VVecEA2. Taken singly this STRENGTHENS _sound (weaker hypothesis) and WEAKENS _cover (weaker conclusion). But _iff is preserved AS AN IFF with its right-hand side `not (bracketOne s0 p s1).holds` textually unchanged, now proved from a strictly weaker carrier, so the deliverable -- a disjunctive-exists-forall formula equivalent to the bracket's negation -- is strictly stronger than before. Stated this way rather than glossed as 'no conclusion changed', which would have been false at the definition level.
declaration_preservation.gate_probe_left_at_the_stronger_shape: MR_dedekind_shape_at_pR still states the HasDedekindINF shape (kplus in the LEFT disjunct). That IMPLIES the faithful carrier's obligation (kplusOpen_of_kplus), and the proof takes Or.inr so the left disjunct is not what is exhibited. Weakening it to match the new carrier would have discarded a theorem to gain nothing. Recorded in its docstring.
